channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: What Does Real-World Use Tell Us About Blu? | #GFN26 Science Lab
item.description: Laboratory data can tell us what a product emits; real-world use tells us how it actually fits into people’s lives. Evidence on blu should therefore be judged not only by product chemistry, but by switching patterns, user behaviour and whether smokers move away from cigarettes completely. That is where harm reduction becomes measurable. The most useful question is not whether a vaping product is perfect, but whether it reduces exposure for adults who would otherwise keep smoking. (Published on September 23, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Bloomberg Tobacco Grants Face Scrutiny as New GSTHR Report Highlights Global Shift to Safer Nicotine
item.description: Bloomberg-funded tobacco control is facing renewed scrutiny at the same time the latest GSTHR report shows a global shift towards safer nicotine use. That contrast matters: billions can be spent resisting products that consumers are already using to move away from cigarettes. Public health should be accountable not only for its intentions, but for whether its influence helps reduce smoking or keeps harm reduction politically inconvenient. (Published on September 23, 2026byvapingpost.com)

item.title: Flaws of Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Studies
item.description: Electronic medical records can look objective while still giving researchers a distorted view of behaviour. Smoking status, vaping history, dual use and switching are often recorded incompletely or reduced to crude categories that miss the timing and direction of change. For nicotine research, those gaps matter because the difference between “ever used” and “switched away from cigarettes” can alter the entire interpretation of risk. Better data means better science — and better science means better policy. (Published on September 23, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: The Policy War on Smoke-Free Alternatives
item.description: Smoke-free alternatives are being pulled into a policy fight that often forgets why they matter in the first place. The issue is not whether nicotine should be celebrated; it is whether adults who smoke are allowed realistic ways to reduce their exposure to burning tobacco. A war on pouches, vapes and other non-combustible products can quickly become a defence of the cigarette by default. Harm reduction asks a simpler question: does the policy make the most dangerous choice easier or harder to leave behind? (Published on September 23, 2026byconsideratepouchers.org)

item.title: Can Nicotine Be Replaced? 6-MN Is Already on the Market While Key Human Evidence Is Still Missing
item.description: A nicotine substitute entering the market before key human evidence is available should make regulators ask better questions, not reach for easy assumptions. New molecules such as 6-methyl nicotine may sit outside familiar tobacco and nicotine frameworks, but that does not make them automatically safer, riskier or irrelevant. The priority should be transparent testing, pharmacology, exposure data and real-world monitoring before public health claims are made. Innovation can support harm reduction only when the evidence keeps pace with the product. (Published on September 23, 2026by2firsts.com)
